# P9.S3 — Combined spec+plan gate for small slices

**Date:** 2026-06-09
**Status:** draft
**Tracker:** P9.S3 (slice of P9 — Review-pipeline efficiency)
**Parent spec:** `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md` (S3 section)
**Depends on:** P9.S1 (done), P9.S2 (done)

## Problem

Every slice in a Superstar-driven project pays for three review gates — spec,
plan, post-slice. The phase baseline (multistore, `external-reviewer stats`,
2026-06-06) shows spec chains averaging ~2.3 rounds and plan chains ~2.7. For a
small, single-surface slice — one tool or skill area, no new subsystem, no new
product decisions — the standalone spec review and the plan review largely
re-examine the same narrow change. The spec gate's rounds are avoidable in that
case: one review that covers both the plan and its (un-reviewed) spec would
catch the same defects at half the early-gate cost.

P9.S1 made each round cheaper (depth defaults, model tiering) and P9.S2 caught
mechanical defects locally before the first paid round (`preflight`). Neither
removed an entire gate. S3 closes that gap for eligible slices by folding the
spec review into the plan review.

## Goal

Let an eligible small slice skip the standalone spec review and instead carry
spec coverage into the plan review, halving the early-gate round count for those
slices without weakening review quality. Concretely:

- A `--combined-gate <spec-path>` flag on `external-reviewer review --kind plan`
  that attaches the un-reviewed spec to the plan review and instructs the
  reviewer to also review the spec, tagging spec-level findings distinctly.
- `chain.json` stamps `combined_gate` + the spec path per round so combined
  chains are identifiable after the fact.
- `external-reviewer stats` segments plan chains into combined vs standalone so
  the phase measurement plan can quantify the saving.
- `brainstorming` and `writing-plans` skill text defines eligibility and routes
  eligible slices through the combined gate.

This is S3 of the phase. It does not change the verdict contract, chain layout,
provider invocation, or any S1/S2 behaviour.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- No combined gate for phase-level specs — phase specs always receive a
  standalone spec review.
- No mechanical eligibility enforcement — eligibility is author judgment guided
  by skill text; the CLI does not gate on it.
- No changes to the verdict contract, chain-folder layout, merged-verdict truth
  table, or provider invocation shape.
- No changes to S1 behaviour (depth defaults, model tiering, resolution gate,
  base stats) or S2 behaviour (preflight) beyond the additive
  `combined_gate` stats segment.
- No consumer-repo (multistore) changes.

## Design

All CLI behaviour lives in
`skills/external-review/scripts/external-reviewer.py`. Skill text lives in
`skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, `skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, and
`skills/external-review/SKILL.md`. Tests live in
`skills/external-review/tests/`. Workflow-step verification touches
`tools/tasktool/` only with a regression test (no production code change
expected).

### S3.a — Eligibility (skill text)

`skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md` (spec flow) and
`skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md` (plan flow) gain a short "Combined spec+plan
gate" section. The combined gate applies to
**slice-level specs only** — a phase-level spec (like the P9 phase design)
always receives a standalone spec review.

A slice may use the combined gate when **all** of these hold:

- **Single-surface change** — one tool/skill/app area; no new subsystem.
- **No cross-repo or cross-plugin impact.**
- **Spec fits the existing phase direction** — no new product decisions that
  would otherwise warrant a standalone spec conversation.

When eligible, `brainstorming` still writes the spec document and commits the
spec artifact transaction, but **skips the standalone external spec review**;
it transitions directly to `writing-plans`. `writing-plans` then invokes the
plan review with `--combined-gate <spec-path>`, so the plan review carries the
spec-coverage burden. The author still sets `--workflow-step plan` after writing
the plan (see S3.c).

Ineligible or uncertain → today's two-gate flow (standalone spec review, then
plan review) unchanged. The skill text frames this as a judgment call with a
bias toward the standard two-gate flow: if any condition is doubtful, do not use
the combined gate.

### S3.b — `--combined-gate <spec-path>` flag

`external-reviewer review --kind plan --combined-gate <path/to/spec.md>` takes
the spec path as its explicit argument.

**Validation** (both surfaced before any chain or reviewer work, matching the
existing early-validation block at the top of the `review` dispatch):

- `--combined-gate` is valid **only with `--kind plan`** — any other kind exits
  **2** with a clear message.
- The spec path **must exist** — a missing path exits **2** with a clear
  message (same exit-2 idiom used today for a missing `--file`/`--context`).

**Context attachment.** The resolved spec path is added to the review's context
set so the spec is attached to the prompt and recorded as a context file. If the
same path was also passed via `--context`, it is **deduplicated** (attached
once) — resolved-path identity is the dedup key. This makes the spec attachment
verifiable from the flag rather than inferred from whatever `--context` happens
to carry (which also carries tracker files).

**Prompt guidance.** When `--combined-gate` is set, the plan `MODE_GUIDANCE` is
augmented with a spec-coverage instruction:

> This plan's spec did not receive a standalone review. Also review the attached
> spec for completeness, internal consistency, and groundedness; tag spec-level
> findings distinctly.

`make_prompt` currently formats `MODE_GUIDANCE[kind]` internally. To thread the
augmentation cleanly, `make_prompt` gains an optional `extra_guidance: str |
None = None` parameter; when set, it is appended to the kind's mode guidance
before formatting. The default (`None`) keeps every existing call byte-identical.
The guidance applies to **every round** of a combined chain (round-1 broad and
incremental follow-ups), since the spec remains un-reviewed throughout.

**Manifest stamp.** Each round entry (the dict assembled near
`external-reviewer.py:3312`) records:

- `combined_gate: true`
- `combined_gate_spec: <repo-relative or absolute spec path as supplied/resolved>`

Standalone plan rounds and all non-plan rounds do **not** carry these keys (or
carry `combined_gate: false` — see Open decisions resolved below), so existing
chains read back unchanged.

### S3.b-stats — Combined-gate segmentation in `stats`

`collect_review_stats` classifies each **plan** chain in the window:

- **combined** if any in-window round has `combined_gate == true`;
- **standalone** otherwise.

A new top-level `combined_gate` block is added to the stats dict:

```
"combined_gate": {
  "combined":   {"chains": <int>, "rounds": <int>},
  "standalone": {"chains": <int>, "rounds": <int>}
}
```

`chains` counts distinct plan chains in each class; `rounds` counts in-window
round entries across those chains (round entries, matching the existing
per-kind `round_count` convention — not reviewer invocations). Only plan chains
are classified; non-plan kinds are not represented in this block.

`print_stats_table` prints one summary line after the per-slice line, e.g.:

```
combined-gate (plan): combined=<chains>c/<rounds>r  standalone=<chains>c/<rounds>r
```

`--json` output carries the same `combined_gate` block. When there are no plan
chains in the window, both classes report zeros (the block is always present
for a stable schema).

### S3.c — Workflow-step compatibility (verify-only)

The combined-gate flow sets `tasktool set <slice-id> --workflow-step plan`
directly from spec-written state, without an intervening spec-review-passed
step. This must not be blocked.

**Verified during this slice's design:** `tools/tasktool` enforces no
step-ordering precondition — `_validate_set_flags`
(`tools/tasktool/commands.py:110-117`) only checks that the supplied step value
is a member of the allowed set for the row kind (slice:
`{spec, plan, implement, done}`). There is no rule requiring the spec step or a
passed spec review before `plan`. So `set --workflow-step plan` from spec state
already works.

S3 therefore makes **no tasktool production change**. It adds a regression test
asserting `tasktool set <slice> --workflow-step plan` succeeds when the row's
current step is `spec` (pinning the no-precondition behaviour against future
drift) and documents the combined-gate step transition in the skill text.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `external-reviewer review --kind plan --combined-gate <spec>` injects the
   spec-coverage guidance into the plan prompt (assertable: the guidance text
   appears in the round-1 request prompt), attaches the spec to the context set
   (deduplicated if also in `--context`), and stamps `combined_gate: true` plus
   the spec path in the `chain.json` round entry.
2. `--combined-gate` with any kind other than `plan` exits **2** without
   spawning a reviewer or creating a chain folder.
3. `--combined-gate <missing-path>` exits **2** without spawning a reviewer or
   creating a chain folder.
4. A standalone plan review (no `--combined-gate`) is byte-identical to today:
   no `combined_gate` guidance in the prompt, and `make_prompt`'s default
   `extra_guidance=None` leaves the assembled prompt unchanged.
5. `external-reviewer stats` (text and `--json`) reports a `combined_gate`
   segment classifying plan chains into combined vs standalone with per-class
   chain and round counts; a fixture with one combined plan chain and one
   standalone plan chain yields `combined: {chains: 1, ...}` and
   `standalone: {chains: 1, ...}`; a window with no plan chains yields zeros in
   both classes.
6. `tasktool set <slice-id> --workflow-step plan` succeeds when the row's
   current `workflow_step` is `spec` (regression test pinning the
   no-precondition behaviour); no tasktool production code changed.
7. `skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, `skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, and
   `skills/external-review/SKILL.md` document the combined-gate eligibility
   rules (slice-only, three conditions), the brainstorming "write spec but skip
   standalone review" branch, the `--combined-gate` invocation in writing-plans,
   and the `--workflow-step plan`-from-spec transition.
8. The existing `skills/external-review/tests/` suite passes, and the new
   behaviours (AC 1–6) are covered by added unit/subprocess tests.

## Open decisions resolved

- **`combined_gate` absent vs `false` on standalone rounds.** Standalone and
  non-plan rounds omit the `combined_gate`/`combined_gate_spec` keys entirely
  (rather than writing `combined_gate: false`). Stats classification treats a
  missing key as not-combined, so absence is unambiguous and keeps existing
  chains byte-stable on read-back. (Either is acceptable for AC1; the spec picks
  omission for minimal manifest churn.)
- **Stats `rounds` unit.** The `combined_gate` segment counts round entries
  (consistent with the per-kind `round_count`), not reviewer invocations. The
  reviewer-invocation count is a per-slice-metric concern (S1.e) and is not
  duplicated here.
- **Guidance scope across rounds.** The combined-gate guidance is applied on
  every round of a combined chain, because the spec stays un-reviewed for the
  life of the chain.

## Risks

- **Quality regression from dropping the standalone spec gate.** Mitigation:
  the combined gate is opt-in and narrowly scoped (single-surface, no new
  product decisions); the plan reviewer is explicitly instructed to review the
  attached spec and tag spec findings distinctly; the post-slice gate
  (unchanged, `thorough`, strong model) remains the safety net; and the phase
  measurement plan watches post-slice revise rate as the canary, segmenting
  combined chains via the new `combined_gate` stamp.
- **Author misjudges eligibility** (uses the combined gate for a slice that
  warranted a standalone spec conversation). Mitigation: skill text biases
  toward the two-gate flow on any doubt; the conditions are conjunctive (all
  must hold); ineligible-but-used cases still get full plan + spec coverage in
  one review, so the failure mode is "slightly less spec scrutiny," not "no
  spec scrutiny."
- **Version skew.** S3 adds a CLI flag and a stats field; shims hard-fail on
  VERSION drift, so the change ships with a version bump and `install.sh` re-run
  per the release process (decided with the user at slice close).

## Spec-coverage map (phase S3 → this spec)

| Phase design item | This spec |
|---|---|
| S3.a eligibility (slice-only, three conditions, brainstorming/writing-plans routing) | S3.a |
| S3.b `--combined-gate <spec-path>`: kind-plan-only exit 2, missing-path exit 2, auto-add to context, MODE_GUIDANCE append, `chain.json` stamp | S3.b |
| Phase: "so stats can segment combined vs standalone chains" | S3.b-stats |
| S3.c workflow-step `plan`-from-spec not blocked (expected no-op) | S3.c |
| Phase AC5 (`--combined-gate` injects guidance, adds context, exits 2 on missing/non-plan, stamps `combined_gate`+spec path) | AC 1–4 |
| Phase AC7 (skill texts reflect combined-gate eligibility) | AC7 |
| Phase AC8 (pytest green + new tests) | AC8 |

# P9 — Review-pipeline efficiency: fewer rounds, cheaper rounds

**Date:** 2026-06-06
**Status:** draft
**Tracker:** P9 (phase)

## Problem

Every slice in a Superstar-driven project pays for three review gates — spec,
plan, post-slice — and each gate usually takes multiple rounds. Measured
baseline from the largest consumer repo (multistore, `external-reviewer stats`,
captured 2026-06-06):

| kind       | rounds | first | follow-up | pass | revise | revise rate |
|------------|--------|-------|-----------|------|--------|-------------|
| spec       | 151    | 66    | 85        | 65   | 51     | 34%         |
| plan       | 172    | 64    | 108       | 62   | 80     | 47%         |
| post-slice | 156    | 69    | 87        | 63   | 73     | 47%         |

That is ~7.3 reviewer rounds per slice (spec 2.3, plan 2.7, post-slice 2.3),
before counting sweep reviewers. A measured round-1 `plan` review at
`--review-depth thorough` (P23.S3 in multistore) consumed ~1.03M total tokens
across primary + sweep (~173k non-cache-read), with both reviewers returning
the same verdict — concordant sweeps on low-risk gates are pure cost.

Two structural observations drive this design:

1. **Round count dominates cost, not round size.** Plan chains average ~1.7
   follow-up rounds. Each `revise` verdict costs a full reviewer run plus a
   local fix cycle. Many revise findings are mechanical (missing acceptance
   gates, dangling file references, placeholder text, tasklist drift) and are
   catchable locally for free.
2. **Redundancy is spent in the wrong place.** Sweeps currently run wherever
   `thorough` is passed, and in practice callers pass `thorough` for spec and
   plan reviews too. The gate where an agent is most likely to have fabricated
   "done" is post-slice; that is where redundancy belongs.

## Goals

- Cut average reviewer rounds per slice from ~7.3 to ≤ 4.5 without weakening
  the post-slice gate.
- Halve spec/plan reviewer invocations (depth defaults + combined gate).
- Catch mechanical revise-class findings locally before the first paid round.
- Make the improvement measurable: `stats --since` comparison against the
  baseline table above.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- No changes to reviewer providers themselves (`codex exec` / `claude --print`
  invocation shape stays, beyond honouring a model override).
- No prompt-template rewrites beyond the combined-gate guidance addition.
- No consumer-repo (multistore) changes; it consumes the updated plugin.
- No changes to the verdict contract, chain folder layout, or merged-verdict
  truth table.

## Design

Three slices, ordered so S1 ships immediately and the trial comparison can
start while S2/S3 land.

### S1 — Quick wins: kind-aware depth defaults, context trimming, resolution gate for all kinds, model tiering, `stats --since`

All changes in `skills/external-review/scripts/external-reviewer.py`,
`skills/external-review/SKILL.md`, `skills/project-setup/scripts/reviewer-agent`,
and the skill texts that invoke reviews (`skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`,
`skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, `skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md`
where they reference review invocation).

**S1.a Kind-aware depth defaults.** `--review-depth` argparse default changes
from `"standard"` to `None` (external-reviewer.py:1851-1852). Resolution order:
explicit flag > kind default. Kind defaults: `spec`/`plan`/`design`/
`implementation`/`other` → `standard`; `post-slice`/`post-phase` → `thorough`.
The resolved depth is recorded per round in `chain.json` (new field
`depth_resolved`) so stats can segment. Skill text examples stop passing
`--review-depth thorough` for spec/plan invocations and document the defaults.
Explicit `--review-depth thorough` on a spec/plan review continues to work
exactly as today (escalation stays one flag away).

**S1.b Context trimming.** Skill text change only: callers pass `tasktool
brief <work-id>` output written to a temp/scratch file (or the phase-filtered
extract) as `--context` instead of the full `docs/tasklist.json`. The
external-review SKILL.md "Context files" section gains a rule: do not pass
files whose bulk is unrelated to the work item; prefer `tasktool brief`.
(Enforcement arrives with S2's preflight size warning.)

**S1.c Resolution gate for all kinds.** The round-N+1 resolution-required gate
(external-reviewer.py:2532-2536) drops its
`args.kind in ("post-slice", "post-phase")` restriction: any kind whose prior
round verdict was `revise` requires `r{N}-resolution.md` before the next round,
with the existing `--allow-missing-resolution` waiver and the existing
process-failure bypass unchanged. Rationale: incremental rounds only converge
fast when the reviewer can verify fixes against a resolution report; spec/plan
chains currently skip this and pay extra rounds re-litigating. SKILL.md
resolution-artifact section updates accordingly. Migration note: existing
chains with a `revise` tail and no resolution file will refuse the next round
until a resolution is written or the waiver is passed — acceptable, the waiver
is the escape hatch.

**S1.d Model tiering.** `reviewer-agent` honours a new optional
`AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` env var: `claude --print --model "$AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL"`
/ `codex exec -m "$AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL"` when set, no flag when unset.
`external-reviewer.py` sets `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` for each reviewer process
from optional env config, per this exact invocation matrix (every round, not
just round 1 — follow-up primaries keep their kind's tier):

| Reviewer invocation                                   | Model env used               |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `spec`/`plan`/`design`/`implementation`/`other` primary, any round | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_LIGHT` |
| `post-slice`/`post-phase` primary, any round          | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_STRONG`|
| Any sweep (first-round or final-ready), any kind      | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_STRONG`|

- The mapped env var being unset → `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` is not exported for
  that invocation; behaviour identical to today. There is no cross-tier
  fallback (LIGHT never substitutes for STRONG or vice versa).
- A per-invocation `--model <name>` flag overrides the matrix for every
  reviewer in that round.
- Accepted trade-off (explicit): at `standard` depth a spec/plan chain's
  decisive `ready` can come from the light model. That is the intended cost
  posture — the post-slice gate (strong model, `thorough`) is the safety net,
  and the measurement plan watches post-slice revise rate as the canary.

The chosen model (or `null`) is recorded in the existing `model` field in
`chain.json` round entries.

**S1.e `stats --since <ISO-date>` + per-slice metric.** `run_stats` gains a
`--since` filter on round `started_at`, so a trial window can be compared
against the historical baseline. Dates are parsed as UTC; a date-only value
means midnight UTC (matching the `utc_now_iso()` timestamps already stored in
`chain.json`). Rounds without timestamps (legacy) are excluded when `--since`
is passed, and the output notes how many were excluded (no silent truncation).

To support the rounds-per-slice goal directly, stats also gains a per-slice
section: chains are grouped by stored `work_id`; the **denominator** is the
count of distinct slice work-ids that have a `post-slice` chain whose latest
round in the window has a passing merged verdict (`ready` / `ready with small
edits`); the **numerator** is all rounds (including sweeps) across the `spec`,
`plan`, and `post-slice` chains of those work-ids. Both numbers and the
resulting rounds-per-slice ratio appear in text and `--json` output.

Correlation requires `work_id` on every gate, so the review-invoking skill
texts (`brainstorming`, `writing-plans`) are updated in this slice to pass
`--work-id <slice-id>` on slice-level `spec` and `plan` reviews whenever a
tasktool row exists (today only `post-slice`/`post-phase` require it; the CLI
already accepts and stores it for all kinds). In-window `spec`/`plan` chains
without a `work_id` are listed as uncorrelated AND flag the ratio: stats
prints/emits `per_slice_complete: false` with a warning that early-gate rounds
may be undercounted, so the ≤ 4.5 figure cannot be claimed from an incomplete
window.

### S2 — Deterministic preflight gate + strengthened self-review checklists

**S2.a `external-reviewer preflight` subcommand.**

```
external-reviewer preflight --kind <kind> --file <target> [--context <path>]...
```

Deterministic checks, no LLM calls:

1. Target exists, non-empty, UTF-8.
2. Placeholder scan: `TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX`, `???`, `lorem ipsum`
   (case-insensitive, whole-token) outside fenced code blocks.
3. Referenced-path check: markdown links and backtick-quoted strings that look
   like repo-relative paths (heuristic: contain `/` and an extension or are
   under a known docs/src dir) must exist on disk, with explicit exemptions —
   anything inside fenced code blocks, paths containing placeholder or glob
   characters (`<`, `>`, `*`, `{`, `}`, `$`, `…`), and paths under
   `docs/reviewer/` (future/generated artifacts) are skipped. Severity split:
   a dangling **markdown link** is a failure; a dangling **backtick path** is
   a warning (prose often cites paths illustratively). Failures list each
   dangling path.
4. Kind-required sections: `plan` → at least one task list and a
   verification/acceptance-gates section; `spec` → acceptance criteria section;
   `post-slice`/`post-phase` → evidence/verification section in the target.
   Section detection is by heading keyword match, tolerant of phrasing
   (`Verification`, `Acceptance`, `Gates`, `Evidence`).
5. Context hygiene: every `--context` file exists; warn (not fail) when any
   context file exceeds 16KB with a hint to pass `tasktool brief` output
   instead (catches the full-`tasklist.json` habit from S1.b).

Output: human-readable findings list + `--emit json`; exit 0 = pass
(warnings allowed), exit 4 = failures present (distinct from the existing
exit 3 resolution-gate code).

**S2.b Auto-preflight on round 1.** `review` runs the same checks in-process
before submitting a round-1 (broad-mode) review and refuses on failure,
printing the findings. `--no-preflight` skips. Incremental rounds (N+1) skip
auto-preflight — the diff/resolution machinery covers them, and re-running
path checks on an already-reviewed document adds friction without catching the
revise drivers.

**S2.c Self-review checklists.** `brainstorming` (spec self-review section)
and `writing-plans` (plan self-review) skill texts gain a short list of the
top historical revise drivers as explicit checks: vague verification steps
("verify it works" without a command), claims not grounded in the repo
(referenced functions/flags that don't exist), tasklist drift (work-id,
status, or dependency mismatches vs `docs/tasklist.json`), and acceptance
criteria that a reviewer cannot evaluate from the document alone. The
checklist instructs running `external-reviewer preflight` before invoking
external review.

### S3 — Combined spec+plan gate for small slices

**S3.a Eligibility (skill text, `brainstorming` + `writing-plans`).** The
combined gate is for slice-level specs only — phase-level specs (like this
one) always receive a standalone spec review. A slice may use the combined
gate when ALL hold:

- Single-surface change (one tool/skill/app area; no new subsystem).
- No cross-repo or cross-plugin impact.
- Spec fits the existing phase direction (no new product decisions).

When eligible, brainstorming still writes the spec but skips the standalone
spec review; writing-plans proceeds immediately, and the plan review carries
the spec-coverage burden. Ineligible or uncertain → today's two-gate flow.

**S3.b `--combined-gate <spec-path>` flag.** `external-reviewer review --kind
plan --combined-gate <path/to/spec.md>` takes the spec path as its explicit
argument: the file must exist (exit 2 otherwise) and is automatically added to
the context set, so the spec attachment is verifiable rather than inferred
from `--context` (which also carries tracker files). The flag appends to the
plan MODE_GUIDANCE: "This plan's spec did not receive a standalone review.
Also review the attached spec for completeness, internal consistency, and
groundedness; tag spec-level findings distinctly." It is valid only with
`--kind plan` (exit 2 otherwise). `chain.json` records `combined_gate: true`
and the spec path per round so `stats` can segment combined vs standalone
chains.

**S3.c Workflow-step compatibility.** `tasktool set <id> --workflow-step plan`
directly from spec-written state must not be blocked by any step-ordering
validation; verify and adjust tasktool only if it enforces spec-review-passed
as a precondition (current behaviour check is an S3 task, expected no-op).

## Acceptance criteria (phase)

1. Omitting `--review-depth` yields `standard` for spec/plan and `thorough`
   for post-slice/post-phase, with `depth_resolved` recorded in `chain.json`;
   explicit flags override.
2. A spec/plan chain whose prior round was `revise` refuses round N+1 without
   `r{N}-resolution.md` (exit 3), waivable with `--allow-missing-resolution`.
3. With `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_LIGHT`/`_STRONG` set, each reviewer process
   receives the model mapped by the S1.d invocation matrix (covering
   first-round primary, follow-up primary, post-slice/post-phase primary,
   first-round sweep, and final-ready sweep) and `chain.json` records it;
   with neither set, invocation is byte-identical to today.
4. `external-reviewer preflight` catches each check-class in a fixture
   document (placeholder, dangling path, missing section, oversized context)
   and passes a known-good document; `review` auto-runs it on round 1 and
   `--no-preflight` skips.
5. `--combined-gate <spec-path>` injects the spec-coverage guidance, adds the
   spec to context, exits 2 when the path is missing or the kind is not
   `plan`, and stamps `combined_gate` plus the spec path in `chain.json`.
6. `stats --since 2026-06-07 --json` returns only rounds started on/after the
   date (UTC), reports the excluded-legacy count, and emits the per-slice
   section: passing-post-slice work-id denominator, all-rounds numerator,
   rounds-per-slice ratio, the uncorrelated-chain list, and the
   `per_slice_complete` flag. Test fixture: a slice with spec, plan, and
   post-slice chains sharing a `work_id` — the numerator includes all three
   kinds' rounds; a variant with a missing spec-chain `work_id` sets
   `per_slice_complete: false` and lists the chain as uncorrelated.
7. All affected skill texts (external-review, brainstorming, writing-plans,
   subagent-driven-development) reflect the new defaults, trimming rule,

- Baseline: the stats table in **Problem** (multistore, captured 2026-06-06).

  baseline 47% (the post-slice gate must not weaken).

  conclusions.

- **Quality regression on spec/plan gates** from losing sweeps and using a
  lighter model. Mitigation: post-slice gate unchanged at `thorough` with the
  strong model; escalation is one explicit flag away; measurement plan watches
  post-slice revise rate as the canary (defects slipping past cheaper early
  gates would surface there).

  the S2.a exemption rules (fenced blocks, placeholder/glob characters,
  `docs/reviewer/` paths), the link-vs-backtick severity split, the

  existing corpus of specs/plans in this repo and multistore.
- **Resolution-gate friction on spec/plan chains** mid-migration. Mitigation:
  existing waiver flag; gate only fires when the prior verdict was `revise`.
- **Version skew**: shims hard-fail on VERSION drift, so S1's CLI changes ship
  with a version bump and `install.sh` re-run per the release process.

1. Findings

F1. Severity: important — The spec says combined-gate guidance applies to every round, but does not define how round N+1 remembers the combined spec if the operator omits `--combined-gate`.
The document requires every combined-chain round to carry the guidance and stamp (`docs/specs/2026-06-09-P9.S3-combined-spec-plan-gate-design.md:125`, `:131`), but AC1 only asserts the round-1 request prompt (`:190-194`). In current code, incremental prompts are built from the current invocation’s `context` and `make_prompt` args (`skills/external-review/scripts/external-reviewer.py:3065`, `:3084-3088`), and the manifest currently has no chain-level field analogous to `work_id` that can restore the spec path on later rounds. This leaves two incompatible implementation paths: “caller must pass the flag every rerun” vs “chain persists and reuses the combined spec.” Without choosing one, round 2 can silently lose spec coverage while stats still classify the chain as combined from round 1.

F2. Severity: minor — The test location / coverage wording is internally inconsistent for AC6.
The design says workflow-step verification touches `tools/tasktool/` with a regression test and no production change expected (`docs/specs/2026-06-09-P9.S3-combined-spec-plan-gate-design.md:62-65`, `:183-186`), but AC8 says AC1-6 are covered by added tests in `skills/external-review/tests/` (`:216-217`). AC6 belongs naturally under `tools/tasktool/tests/`, because `_validate_set_flags` and `cmd_set` live in `tools/tasktool/commands.py` (`tools/tasktool/commands.py:80-125`, `:1223-1234`). As written, an implementer could satisfy one sentence and violate the other.

2. Open questions / assumptions

- Should `--combined-gate` be required on every follow-up review invocation, or should the first round persist `combined_gate_spec` at chain level and auto-apply it on later rounds?
- If the path is persisted, should a later explicit `--combined-gate <different-spec>` be rejected as a chain mismatch, similar to stored `work_id` mismatch handling?

3. Suggested document edits

- In S3.b, add a “Follow-up rounds” paragraph choosing one behavior. Recommended: persist `combined_gate_spec` at chain level on round 1; later plan rounds in that chain auto-apply the same guidance/context/stamp; an explicit different spec path exits 6 or 2 with a clear mismatch error.
